status: FROZEN - do not edit. Any change goes to results/deviations.md (timestamped) before the affected statistic is computed.
purpose: Small falsifiable checks supporting idea cards I1 (energy inventories) and I2 (European power and gas). Mechanism checks only: no strategy backtest, no parameter chosen from results.
prior_exposure: EIA weekly inventories (WCESTUS1, Cushing, gas storage NW2) and NYMEX contracts 1-4 were used on 2026-10-22 for a different hypothesis (inventory-driven calendar spreads). No release-day statistic, no inventory-surprise vs return statistic, no cloud-cover statistic, and no ENTSO-E or AGSI+ data have been computed or viewed before this freeze.

common.trading_days: Dates with a non-missing contract-1 settlement in the market's EIA daily series.
common.front_return: r_t = ln(C1_t / C1_{t-1}); on the first trading day after a front-contract expiry, r_t = ln(C1_t / C2_{t-1}) so that both prices refer to the same contract.

expiry_rules.WTI: Last trading day = 3 business days before the 25th calendar day of the month preceding delivery; if the 25th is not a business day, 3 business days before the last business day preceding the 25th.
expiry_rules.NG: Last trading day = 3 business days before the first calendar day of the delivery month.

common.holidays: US federal holidays (pandas USFederalHolidayCalendar) for release-date shifts; business days for expiries = trading days observed in the data.

release_calendar.WTI_WPSR: Week ending Friday F (index of WCESTUS1): release R = F + 5 days (Wednesday); R = F + 6 days if a US federal holiday falls between F + 3 and F + 5 inclusive. Week dropped if R is not a trading day.
release_calendar.NG_WNGSR: Week ending Friday F (index of NW2_EPG0_SWO_R48_BCFw): release R = F + 6 days (Thursday); R = F + 5 days if F + 6 is a US federal holiday. Week dropped if R is not a trading day.
release_calendar.note: Approximate calendar (a few weeks per year may be misdated); misdating biases every test toward no effect. Rule not changed after any statistic is computed.

common.coverage_audit_first: Before any statistic: row counts by year for every series, list of gaps longer than 5 business days, written to results/coverage.md. NG sample rule fixed now: if RNGC1 or RNGC2 has a gap longer than 5 business days, the NG sample starts on the first trading day after the last such gap.
common.hac: Newey-West, Bartlett kernel; lags stated per test.
common.bootstrap: Week-block bootstrap: resample calendar weeks (Monday-Sunday) with replacement, 5,000 draws, numpy default_rng(20261023).
common.multiplicity: Primary verdicts: T1-WTI, T1-NG, T2-WTI, T2-NG (4). Holm-adjusted one-sided p-values are reported next to each verdict for information; verdict rules below are unchanged. T3 is exploratory. T4 and T5 are mechanism checks.
common.run_once: Each test script is run once on the full period after the coverage audit. Re-runs are allowed only for crashes or data-integrity fixes logged in results/deviations.md; all runs are logged in results/trial_log.csv.
common.reporting: Every verdict is reported whatever the result (repo README and deck annex).

tests.name: Release-day volatility of energy futures
tests.hypothesis: Absolute daily returns of front-month futures are larger on scheduled EIA release days than on other trading days: the weekly print carries information the market did not have.

data.WTI: EIA RCLC1d and RCLC2d (NYMEX WTI contracts 1-2, daily settlement)
data.NG: EIA RNGC1d and RNGC2d (NYMEX Henry Hub contracts 1-2, daily settlement)
data.calendars: Week-ending dates of EIA WCESTUS1w (crude) and NW2_EPG0_SWO_R48_BCFw (gas storage)

tests.statistic: ratio = mean |r| on release days / mean |r| on all other trading days; 95% CI and one-sided p (share of draws <= 1) from the week-block bootstrap.
tests.prediction: ratio > 1 for WTI (Wednesday prints) and for NG (Thursday prints).
tests.verdict_rule: Per market: SUPPORTED if the 95% CI lower bound > 1.00; otherwise NOT SUPPORTED.
secondary_reported_no_prediction: Cross placebo: WTI ratio on NG release days; NG ratio on WTI release days.

tests.name: Direction of the inventory surprise
tests.hypothesis: The unexpected part of the weekly inventory change moves the front contract in the opposite direction on the release day (more stock than expected -> lower price).

data.WTI: EIA WCESTUS1w (US commercial crude stocks excl. SPR, thousand barrels) + WTI front returns as in T1
data.NG: EIA NW2_EPG0_SWO_R48_BCFw (Lower-48 working gas, Bcf) + NG front returns as in T1

tests.surprise_model_M0: Weekly change D_t = I_t - I_{t-1}. OLS of D_t on [1, D_{t-1}, D_{t-2}, sin(2*pi*k*doy/365.25), cos(2*pi*k*doy/365.25)], doy = day of year of F_t, k = 1..2 for crude and k = 1..3 for gas. Expanding window on weeks with week-ending date < F_t only; first forecast after 260 weeks of history. Surprise s_t = D_t - forecast_t; z_t = s_t / sd(s) over the test sample.
tests.period: Release days in [2010-01-04, 2024-04-05] with an available forecast (NG starts later if its history is shorter).
tests.statistic: OLS r_R = a + b * z_t on release days; Newey-West t with 4 lags; Spearman correlation reported.
tests.prediction: b < 0 for WTI and for NG.
tests.verdict_rule: Per market: SUPPORTED if t_b <= -2.0; otherwise NOT SUPPORTED, with the interpretation fixed now: the market's expectation also uses the API survey (Tuesday 16:30 ET) and analyst consensus, which M0 does not have, so the test bounds what a naive expectation captures.
secondary_reported_no_prediction: Sign hit rate: share of release days with sign(r_R) = -sign(s_t).

tests.name: Cloud cover over Cushing (exploratory)
tests.hypothesis: When clouds hide Cushing from optical satellites in the days before the print, more information is left for the release day: |release-day return| is larger in cloudy weeks.
tests.data: Open-Meteo Historical Weather API (ERA5-based archive), hourly cloud_cover (%), point 35.985 N, -96.767 E, UTC.
tests.definitions: C_t = mean hourly cloud_cover over 16:00-19:00 UTC (around the Sentinel-2 overpass) on the 7 calendar days ending the day before WTI release R_t. Cloudy_t = 1 if C_t is in the top tercile of C over the sample, 0 otherwise. RV20_t = sqrt(mean r^2 over the 20 trading days ending the day before R_t).
tests.statistic: OLS |r_R| = a + b * Cloudy_t + c * ln(RV20_t); Newey-West t with 4 lags. Also ratio of mean |r_R| top vs bottom tercile with week-block bootstrap CI.
tests.verdict_rule: CONSISTENT if one-sided t_b >= 1.65; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE AT DAILY RESOLUTION. Never presented as evidence of a trading edge; deck annex unless CONSISTENT.
tests.limitations: Close-to-close returns include other news; vendors also use radar, which clouds do not block; one hub only.

tests.name: Merit order in German day-ahead prices
tests.hypothesis: A higher forecast share of wind and solar in next-day load lowers the day-ahead price.
tests.data: ENTSO-E Transparency Platform, bidding zone DE-LU (EIC 10Y1001A1001A82H): day-ahead prices (A44); day-ahead generation forecast for wind and solar (A69, processType A01: solar, wind onshore, wind offshore); day-ahead total load forecast (A65, processType A01).
tests.definitions: Daily means over the delivery day in Europe/Berlin time (60- or 15-minute resolution averaged). S_d = (solar + wind onshore + wind offshore forecast) / load forecast.
tests.integrity_checks_before_statistic: Row counts per year, units (EUR/MWh, MW), time zone, zone code, share of days with complete data; logged in results/coverage.md.
tests.statistic: OLS P_d = month-year fixed effects + weekday fixed effects + b * S_d; Newey-West t with 7 lags.
tests.verdict_rule: SUPPORTED if t_b <= -5.0; otherwise NOT SUPPORTED.
secondary_reported_no_prediction: b and its t by calendar year.

tests.name: EU gas storage withdrawals and temperature
tests.hypothesis: Cold days drive EU storage withdrawals: net withdrawal rises with heating degree days.
tests.data: GIE AGSI+ API, EU aggregate, daily injection and withdrawal (GWh/d), gasInStorage and full (%); Open-Meteo Historical Weather API daily temperature_2m_mean for Berlin (52.52, 13.405), Paris (48.857, 2.352), Milan (45.464, 9.19), Amsterdam (52.37, 4.895), Vienna (48.208, 16.373), Warsaw (52.23, 21.012), equal weights.
tests.period: Gas days 2015-01-01..2025-12-31; statistic on November-March gas days only.
tests.definitions: NW_d = withdrawal - injection; T_d = mean of the six city temperatures; HDD_d = max(0, 15.5 - T_d).
tests.statistic: OLS NW_d = gas-year fixed effects + weekday fixed effects + b * HDD_d; Newey-West t with 7 lags.
tests.verdict_rule: SUPPORTED if t_b >= 5.0; otherwise NOT SUPPORTED.
